channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Refrigeration hack hits about 700 French supermarkets; France’s cyber agency now names Copeland as well as Danfoss
item.category: Top Story
item.description: Attackers remotely forced refrigeration controllers at French supermarkets into defrost over the nights of 11–13 October, pushing cabinets toward 50°C, starting fires at some stores and spoiling stock. France’s finance minister put the toll at about 700 of 10,000 supermarkets, across Intermarché, Carrefour, Monoprix, Coopérative U and E.Leclerc. CERT-FR named Danfoss AK-series controllers, then added Copeland’s Dixell XWEB systems; both vendors say most affected units are older, end-of-life models. SecurityWeek reports defrost cycles were stretched from one hour to as many as eight, delaying alarms. No group, ransom demand, entry route or CVE is confirmed. The Paris prosecutor is investigating, and on 16 October CERT-FR warned that campaigns are probably still ongoing, so operators of similar controllers elsewhere should treat this as a live warning. - AP via News4JAX (13 Oct 2026); Reuters via The Star (14 Oct 2026); Cybernews; IBTimes citing Le Monde (13 Oct 2026); SecurityWeek (15 Oct 2026) and Industrial Cyber (13 Oct 2026); Danfoss statement (12 Oct 2026); Claroty Team82 research (Aug 2026) - Attacks on the nights of 11–13 Oct 2026; updated 16 Oct 2026 (CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 v3, 16 Oct: campaigns probably still ongoing; Reuters 13 Oct: 4,500+ Danfoss interfaces on Shodan; SecurityWeek: CERT-FR adds Copeland/Dixell; Sekoia: other EU countries) — investigation ongoing

item.title: [Medium] Extortion group n0n claims data from 38 port, shipping and logistics firms; none has confirmed
item.category: Incident (claimed) — extortion group n0n lists 38 maritime and logistics organizations on its leak site; unverified, no victim confirmation, no operational disruption reported
item.description: SOCRadar reported on 13 October, and Industrial Cyber on 15 October, that n0n, an extortion group first seen in September 2026, listed 38 maritime and logistics organizations across 18 countries on its leak site, including container terminals, shipping lines and port IT providers; twelve are in South Korea. The group says it holds vessel schedules, container manifests, gate records and terminal-system configuration files, and reportedly seeks $2.4–14 million per victim. The group usually enters with infostealer-harvested credentials and mostly steals data rather than encrypting it. SOCRadar suggests the batch may trace to one shared application or vulnerability rather than 38 separate intrusions. Nothing is verified: no listed organization has confirmed an incident, and no control-system compromise or disruption is reported. A shared publication deadline of 19 October should show how much is real. - SOCRadar analysis as reported by Industrial Cyber (15 Oct 2026) - Listings reported 15 Oct 2026; leak deadline 19 Oct 2026 — claims unverified

item.title: [Critical] A third Citrix NetScaler zero-day is exploited, and a fourth critical flaw was patched on 9 October
item.category: Incident — three NetScaler zero-days confirmed exploited, state-sponsored actors suspected by Mandiant (not attributed); a fourth critical flaw patched 9 Oct, no exploitation reported
item.description: Citrix has confirmed a third NetScaler zero-day under attack, days after patching two others that were exploited for weeks before disclosure, and on 9 October it shipped a fourth fix. The exploited trio is CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772 and CVE-2026-88779; the federal KEV deadline for the newest passed on 7 October. The earlier pair brought web shells, rogue admin accounts and stolen configurations, and patching does not evict an intruder. The new CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS v4.0 9.5) is a SAML memory overflow that could allow code execution; no exploitation is reported, but appliances patched last week need another upgrade. Shadowserver counts more than 20,000 internet-exposed NetScaler fingerprints. Because NetScaler often fronts remote access into plant networks, an unhunted appliance is a possible foothold toward OT. - Citrix security bulletins CTX697096 and CTX697174 (and the 9 Oct bulletin for CVE-2026-107406); CISA KEV catalog; Dutch NCSC; Tenable, watchTowr, LevelBlue, Arctic Wolf and Mandiant/GTIG research; reported by SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, Cybersecurity Dive and Help Net Security - Fourth flaw CVE-2026-107406 patched 9 Oct 2026, no exploitation reported (The Hacker News, 9 Oct); CVE-2026-88779 fixed 3–4 Oct and added to KEV 4 Oct 2026 (deadline 7 Oct, now passed); watchTowr denial-of-service finding and CISA/Australian warnings 5 Oct 2026 (SecurityWeek and The Record, 5 Oct); first two flaws confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026, mass exploitation after a 28 Sep proof-of-concept write-up; post-exploitation analysis 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Ahold Delhaize reports a cybersecurity incident that took down Albert Heijn, Delhaize and all five US banners’ websites
item.category: Incident — Ahold Delhaize confirms a cybersecurity incident disrupting Albert Heijn and Delhaize online services in the Netherlands and Belgium; store-level OT impact not confirmed; no actor named
item.description: Ahold Delhaize said a cybersecurity incident began on Sunday 11 October, and it switched off some systems as a precaution. Albert Heijn websites, apps and customer service were unavailable, online deliveries paused and loyalty systems stopped; press reports add that some electronic shelf labels showed the previous week’s promotional prices. Delhaize customers in Belgium could not place new online orders. Albert Heijn’s chief executive told broadcaster NOS that work came to a complete standstill at some distribution centres, leaving gaps on shelves; they were running again by 14 October and stores were being restocked on 16 October, while the online store stays down until next week. Cybersecurity Dive reported on 12 October that the websites of all five Ahold Delhaize USA banners (Hannaford, Stop & Shop, Giant Food, Food Lion and The Giant Company) were also down; the company has not said whether in-store operations were affected, and US store impact beyond the websites is reported but unverified. The company is investigating and putting customer, employee and partner data first; the Dutch NCSC found no link to the French refrigeration attack (Euronews, 14 October). The company says stores remain open and it has no evidence customer or associate data was stolen. No actor has been named, and nothing public links the incident to the French refrigeration attacks, so the two are treated as separate for now. - Ahold Delhaize statements as reported by Hackread (12 Oct 2026), Cybersecurity Dive (12 Oct 2026), The Record and SecurityWeek (13 Oct 2026) - Disruption began Sun 11 Oct 2026; reported 12 Oct 2026 — investigation ongoing

item.title: [Critical] Colorado confirms foreign hackers altered pumps and disabled alarms at two small water systems
item.category: Incident — confirmed foreign intrusion into two small, privately owned drinking-water systems; pumping cycles and alarms altered; no known impact to treatment or public safety; actors unidentified; no new development since disclosure
item.description: Colorado Governor Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned water systems in late August, changing equipment settings, disabling remote access and alarms, and altering pumping cycles. Officials describe the disruption as brief, with no known impact to treatment, water quality or public safety, and say they cannot yet confirm which foreign actors were responsible. A separately tracked, broader Iran-linked campaign against US water systems has not been formally connected to this incident. With the French refrigeration attack (top story), it is one of two confirmed OT-tampering incidents in this edition; nothing new has been reported since the initial disclosure. - Colorado Governor’s office statement (18 Sep 2026), reported by Axios Denver and Industrial Cyber (22 Sep) - Intrusions late Aug 2026; confirmed 18 Sep 2026 — no new development as of this edition

item.title: [High] Hackers reached a US-bound tanker’s propulsion system, Bloomberg reports; the FBI says there was no disruption
item.category: Incident — Bloomberg reports, citing unnamed US officials, that hackers temporarily reached the propulsion system of the US-bound tanker VL Prosperity; FBI on record: no operational disruption, instability or crew danger; actor, duration and extent of control unknown; a second tanker was boarded in the Gulf of Mexico
item.description: Bloomberg reported on 2 October, citing US officials who asked not to be named, that FBI and Coast Guard investigators found hackers had temporarily accessed the propulsion system of the very large crude carrier VL Prosperity as it approached the Texas coast this summer. Neither agency has confirmed that finding on the record. The FBI’s on-record statement says there are no reports of operational disruption, vessel instability, danger to crews or environmental impact, and Bloomberg says it is unclear how long the access lasted or what the intruders could control. No one has been publicly blamed. VL Prosperity was boarded in the Atlantic on 21 August after it lost communications, and a second, unnamed tanker was boarded in the Gulf of Mexico days later. On 6 October a federal official told BankInfoSecurity that both boarded tankers were reached through known, unpatched flaws in onboard systems (single unnamed-official account, not independently confirmed). - Bloomberg (citing unnamed US officials), via Supply Chain Brain and gCaptain; FBI statement; boarding details per the US Coast Guard, Dragos and Reuters - Boardings 21 and 24 Aug 2026; propulsion-system access reported 2 Oct 2026; unpatched-flaw detail reported 6 Oct 2026 (BankInfoSecurity)

item.title: [High] Ivanti warns attackers chained three zero-day flaws, one still unpatched, to take root on fully patched Connect Secure VPNs
item.category: Incident — Ivanti Connect Secure VPN zero-day chain exploited on fully patched appliances since early Oct; new actor UTA0576 tracked by Volexity; one flaw still unpatched; no OT victim named
item.description: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that a small number of customers were hit through a chain of three zero-day flaws that gave unauthenticated, root-level code execution on fully patched Connect Secure appliances. Volexity, which found it while investigating a customer incident, dates its case to 3 October (other researchers saw activity from 1 October) and tracks a previously undocumented actor, UTA0576. The intruders stole domain credentials stored on the appliance, searched Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, sprayed passwords and scanned internal networks, but left no web shell or backdoor. Volexity judges, with low confidence, that the group is financially motivated, and, with medium confidence, that it uses AI models for exploit development. Fixes cover two of the flaws (CVE-2026-104935); the third, a privilege-escalation bug, is still unpatched. VPN gateways like this commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary. - Ivanti advisory and Volexity research, as reported by SecurityWeek (13 Oct 2026) - Disclosed 13 Oct 2026; added to CISA KEV 13 Oct 2026; exploitation observed from 3 Oct 2026 — third flaw still unpatched

item.title: [High] FBI and Secret Service say the FortiBleed campaign against Fortinet VPN gateways is still running
item.category: Incident — FBI and Secret Service re-warn that the “FortiBleed” credential-harvesting campaign against internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways remains active; reused or leaked credentials, no CVE; no OT victim named
item.description: The FBI and US Secret Service warned on 6 October that attackers are still scanning internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways with credentials harvested earlier in the campaign. First documented in June, it had collected more than 86,000 working device credentials across 194 countries by 19 June, according to The Hacker News. No vulnerability is involved: the attackers rely on reused or leaked passwords, interception of login traffic and cracking of weakly stored hashes. Some victims were locked out when attackers created new admin accounts, then deleted or reset the legitimate ones; the FBI also says the chain has served as an entry point for ransomware affiliates, and the agencies say targets span all 16 US critical-infrastructure sectors, including energy and food and agriculture. Researchers describe a Russian-speaking operator that may be selling access, with overlaps to INC and Lynx ransomware; that attribution is reported, not confirmed. Fortinet gateways often sit at the IT/OT boundary. - FBI and US Secret Service warning, reported by The Hacker News, BleepingComputer and The Record; CISA mitigation guidance (June 2026) - Ongoing — re-warned 6 Oct 2026; SecurityWeek follow-up on admin lockouts 8 Oct 2026; campaign first documented June 2026

item.title: [Info] Nozomi: the French fridge attacks show why internet-reachable OT control interfaces are a standing risk
item.category: Research — Nozomi Networks analysis of the French refrigeration attacks and internet-exposed OT; no CVE
item.description: Nozomi Networks published an analysis on 13 October arguing that the French supermarket refrigeration attacks illustrate the danger of exposed remote access: anyone who reaches a control interface can issue commands with physical effect. It cites outside counts of thousands of internet-exposed Danfoss systems. Recommendations include removing remote access that is not needed, putting necessary access behind gateways with strong authentication, keeping an inventory of devices and firmware, monitoring for abnormal commands, and clarifying contractor responsibilities. It is vendor analysis and does not name the attacker or entry route. - Nozomi Networks blog - Published 13 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] Booz Allen: AI models went from a perimeter foothold to commands on industrial controllers in about 16 minutes in a lab
item.category: Research — Booz Allen lab test of frontier AI models against a simulated factory network; no CVE
item.description: Booz Allen published results on 8 October from its OT cybersecurity lab, a multi-vendor mock-up of a manufacturing site. Across eight scenarios, frontier AI models met every test objective without source code, engineering documents or OT-specific guidance; in one run a model moved a robotic arm. Firewalls, segmentation and endpoint protection slowed some actions but no single control stopped the models consistently, while a controller that rejected a stop command and a motor in local-control mode held up. This was an isolated lab, and human operators approved every exploit and any action with physical effect, so it shows speed and adaptability, not an observed attack. - Booz Allen Hamilton research - Published 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] MITRE ATT&CK v20 catalogs the Minnesota water-utility PLC attacks and an AI-assisted Mexican government intrusion
item.category: Research — MITRE ATT&CK v20 adds ICS techniques and two critical-infrastructure campaigns; no CVE
item.description: MITRE released ATT&CK v20 on 16 October. It adds campaign C0066, covering internet-facing PLC attacks on more than 30 Minnesota water and wastewater utilities that locked operators out of their own systems (not formally attributed), and C0064, an AI-assisted intrusion across Mexican government bodies that reached a municipal water utility. The ICS matrix gains a consolidated command-and-scripting technique (T1701), DNS and publish/subscribe protocol command-and-control sub-techniques, and a mitigation limiting software installation on ICS assets; the software list adds IOControl, malware linked to CyberAv3ngers. These are analyst catalog entries describing earlier activity, not new attacks, but they give defenders shared detection and mapping language. - Industrial Cyber; MITRE ATT&CK - Released 16 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] FBI takes down domains behind Flax Typhoon’s scanning and phishing tools used against energy and airport targets
item.category: Threat Intelligence — FBI seizes domains behind the MicroScan and FishHub tooling of China-linked Flax Typhoon; joint FBI, CISA, NSA advisory lists power, gas and airport targets; no OT compromise confirmed
item.description: On 8 October the FBI announced it had seized domains used to run two hacking tools, MicroScan and FishHub, attributed to the China-linked group tracked as Flax Typhoon (also Ethereal Panda). MicroScan is a Python scanner with more than 1,300 testing scripts, used alongside a Mirai botnet; FishHub handles spear-phishing, malware delivery and data theft. A joint FBI, CISA and NSA advisory (AA26-281A) with international partners lists targets that include a South Carolina power company, airports in Japan and Poland, and Taiwanese gas and electricity firms, though the FBI did not confirm those were breached. Confirmed compromises are limited to Taiwanese universities. The advisory names older vulnerabilities such as CVE-2019-11510 (Pulse Secure VPN) and CVE-2021-22205 (GitLab). Authorities tie the actor to China-based Integrity Technology Group; they note not all activity may be linked to it. No operational-technology intrusion is described. CISA has since added five of the older flaws the group exploited to its KEV catalog, with an 11 October federal deadline. - FBI action and joint FBI/CISA/NSA advisory AA26-281A, reported by BleepingComputer, The Hacker News and Industrial Cyber - Announced 8 Oct 2026; KEV additions with 11 Oct deadline reported 9 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Palo Alto Networks patches a PAN-OS zero-day that gives root through the management interface; CISA lists it as exploited
item.category: Advisory — Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS management-interface remote code execution (CVE-2026-0322, CVSS 8.6), exploited in “very limited” attacks; added to CISA KEV
item.description: Palo Alto Networks disclosed on 14 October that CVE-2026-0322 lets an attacker who already has credentials and network reach to the PAN-OS management interface run code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and Panorama appliances. The company reports very limited exploitation and published three attacker IP addresses; Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected. Fixes cover PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2, with the 11.2.16 build due on 15 October, and there is no workaround beyond limiting management access to trusted internal addresses. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a federal deadline of 17 October. Firewalls like these often sit on the IT/OT boundary, so a management interface reachable from corporate networks or the internet is the exposure to remove. BleepingComputer did not get answers on who is behind the attacks or whether intruders moved further inside. - BleepingComputer (14 Oct 2026), citing the Palo Alto Networks advisory and CISA’s KEV catalog - Disclosed 14 Oct 2026; KEV deadline 17 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] CISA flags six vulnerabilities in the Eclipse Milo OPC UA library used across energy, water, chemical and manufacturing
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICSA-26-288-01: six flaws in the open-source Eclipse Milo OPC UA stack; no exploitation reported
item.description: CISA published advisory ICSA-26-288-01 on 15 October covering six flaws in Eclipse Milo, an open-source Java OPC UA client and server stack that vendors embed in industrial gateways, historians and SCADA software. The worst, CVE-2026-60007, is a padding-oracle weakness in username-token handling rated 9.1 under CVSS v4.0; the others score between 6.9 and 8.8. Versions up to 1.1.4 are affected, and the fix is Milo 1.1.5 or later. CISA reports no known exploitation. Because the library is bundled inside other products, owners may not know they run it, so the practical work is asking vendors whether their OPC UA components use Milo. The advisory header says five flaws but lists six CVEs. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-288-01; Security Boulevard daily OT roundup - Published 15 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Siemens, Rockwell and ABB release October fixes: critical flaws in S7-1500 CPUs, Industrial Edge and ArmorBlock
item.category: Advisory — October ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens (17 advisories), Rockwell 1732E ArmorBlock, Schneider Electric, ABB dynovaPRO; no exploitation reported; CVE/CVSS not verified
item.description: SecurityWeek’s 14 October roundup says Siemens published 17 advisories. Three are rated critical: certain Simatic S7-1500 CPUs (which inherit hundreds of flaws in an embedded Linux subsystem), Industrial Edge devices, and the Ruggedcom Crossbow Station Access Controller; several others are high, covering Simatic IPC, WinCC, Desigo and more. Rockwell fixed two flaws in the 1732E ArmorBlock I/O module, including a critical one that lets an unauthenticated attacker change the web-server password and take over the admin account. Schneider listed high-severity issues in Pro-face/Harmony HMIs and Sage RTUs. ABB disclosed a dynovaPRO password-reset flaw and said logs show 26 password changes across 9 customers that could be testing; it knows of no exploitation. We could not verify CVE IDs or scores, so none are given. - SecurityWeek, ICS Patch Tuesday (14 Oct 2026), summarizing Siemens ProductCERT, Rockwell, Schneider Electric, ABB and CISA releases - Released 14 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] CISA warns of a critical flaw in end-of-life Hitachi Energy RTU500 firmware that allows unauthenticated firmware uploads
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICSA-26-279-06, Hitachi Energy RTU500 series CMU firmware (substation/utility remote terminal units); reported critical, unauthenticated firmware upload; end-of-life firmware branch; no known exploitation reported
item.description: On 6 October CISA published ICSA-26-279-06 for the CMU firmware of Hitachi Energy’s RTU500 series, widely used as remote terminal units in substations and other utility field sites. A digest of the release describes a critical flaw in an end-of-life firmware branch that lets an unauthenticated party upload firmware, which would mean arbitrary code on a device that talks to the control center. The same release also covered Hitachi Energy Asset Suite, SOI and REB500. We have not confirmed a CVSS score or CVE IDs from the advisory itself, so none are given here; check the advisory for affected versions. CISA reports no known exploitation in the digest we reviewed. End-of-life status matters: if your fleet runs the affected branch, the fix may be migration rather than a patch. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-279-06 (bulletin of six advisories, 6 Oct 2026), relayed by the IT/OT Security Weekly digest (11 Oct 2026) - Released 6 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] BeyondTrust patches a Remote Support zero-day exploited since late August by a suspected China-nexus espionage actor
item.category: Advisory — BeyondTrust Remote Support authentication-bypass zero-day (BT26-05), exploited since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor; vendor remote-access tooling often used to reach plant systems; no OT victims named
item.description: BeyondTrust has fixed CVE-2026-102764, an authentication bypass in self-hosted Remote Support appliances (version 26.2.3 and earlier) that lets an unprivileged remote attacker perform file operations. Mandiant and Google’s threat-intelligence group link the exploitation to a suspected state-sponsored espionage actor they track as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221); CrowdStrike calls it Warp Panda. After getting in, the intruders used web shells, escalated to root, wiped logs and harvested stored credentials for lateral movement. SaaS customers were patched on 8 October; self-hosted customers must patch themselves. Shadowserver counts more than 1,400 exposed instances, and Google expects opportunistic exploitation to follow. No victims are named, and none is reported in critical infrastructure. Integrators and OEMs often use this class of tool for vendor access to plants, so its owners should check it. We did not find a CVSS score, so none is given. - BleepingComputer (16 Oct 2026); The Record; BeyondTrust advisory BT26-05; Mandiant/GTIG and CrowdStrike research as relayed by these outlets - Reported 16 Oct 2026; exploitation since late Aug 2026; SaaS patched 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] CISA flags a critical remote-code-execution flaw in Grid Protection Alliance’s openPDC and openHistorian grid-data software
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICSA-26-281-02, Grid Protection Alliance openPDC and openHistorian (energy-sector grid data software); CVSS v3 9.8 as reported; no known exploitation
item.description: On 8 October CISA published ICSA-26-281-02, covering several classes of high-severity vulnerabilities in the Grid Protection Alliance’s openPDC and openHistorian, open-source software that utilities use to collect and store time-series grid measurements (our description; CISA lists the energy sector). The most serious, CVE-2026-100730, is a deserialization flaw that can give an unauthenticated network attacker remote code execution, which CISA scores CVSS v3.1 9.8; fixes are in openPDC 2.9.482 and openHistorian 2.8.585. CISA reports no known public exploitation. The relevance for OT teams is that these servers sit between substation or phasor data sources and control-center analytics, so a flaw there is a possible stepping stone between networks rather than a direct control-loop risk. Affected versions and fixes are listed in the advisory and are not repeated here. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-281-02, relayed by the Viakoo/Security Boulevard Daily OT Security News roundup (9 Oct 2026) - Released 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Two threat-intel firms report exploitation attempts against SonicWall’s maximum-severity SMA1000 flaw, days after hotfixes shipped
item.category: Advisory — SonicWall rates CVE-2026-102255, an SSRF in the SMA1000 Appliance WorkPlace interface, as maximum severity; unauthenticated and remote; two threat-intel firms report exploitation attempts (not confirmed successful); not in CISA KEV as of 12 Oct
item.description: Previdian and Defused both report their honeypots receiving requests consistent with CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS 10), a pre-authentication server-side request forgery in the SMA1000 WorkPlace interface that SonicWall patched on 6 October; Defused dates its first hits to 8 October (SecurityWeek, 12 October). Neither has determined whether any attempt succeeded, and SonicWall’s advisory did not flag active exploitation. Fixed builds are 12.5.0-03082 and 12.4.3-03670. The flaw is reachable remotely without authentication on SMA1000 6210, 7210 and 8200v models; SMA100 and firewall SSL-VPN are not affected. Shadowserver counts more than 400 exposed SMA1000 appliances. The same interface was hit by SSRF flaws in July and September that were exploited, so quick scanning after a patch is plausible. These gateways often give vendors and integrators a path toward plant networks. - SonicWall advisory SNWLID-2026-0017; Previdian and Defused honeypot observations, reported by SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer; Shadowserver exposure data - Exploitation attempts reported 9–12 Oct 2026 (first seen 8 Oct); hotfixes released 6 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] Industry coalition asks CISA for a binding directive on OT security inside federal agencies
item.category: Policy — OT Cybersecurity Coalition urges CISA to issue a binding operational directive on OT security at federal agencies; a proposal only, no CISA commitment; no CVE
item.description: The OT Cybersecurity Coalition is urging CISA to issue a Binding Operational Directive focused solely on operational technology at federal civilian agencies, CyberScoop reported on 6 October. The coalition wants each agency to name an accountable OT cybersecurity officer, meet minimum practices drawn from existing federal guidance and CISA’s 2022 Cybersecurity Performance Goals, and consider whether NSA’s OT guidance should apply to civilian agencies. It points to a 30 September GAO report finding that only 7 of 22 civilian agencies fully met OMB’s requirements for networked IoT and OT devices, and to this summer’s water-utility attacks. CISA did not respond to CyberScoop and has announced no directive. In our assessment, a directive would bind only federal agencies but would signal what CISA expects of OT programs generally. - OT Cybersecurity Coalition paper, reported by CyberScoop; GAO-26-108937 - Reported 6 Oct 2026; GAO report 30 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] FERC staff publish CIP audit lessons: unregistered new generation, stacked low-impact systems and AI tools in CIP networks
item.category: Regulation — FERC staff report on CIP audit lessons learned flags late registration of new generation, aggregated low-impact systems and AI tools inside CIP networks; no CVE
item.description: On 13 October FERC released a staff report drawing on its fiscal-2026 audits of NERC-registered entities. Most cybersecurity processes reviewed met the mandatory CIP standards, but auditors found three recurring problems. Some generator owners registered new resources late or never identified their BES Cyber Systems, and several inverter-based resources were running commercially without the required cyber evaluation, one more than a year past the threshold. Two entities treated systems as low impact that together met the medium-impact criteria once affiliate and contractor control was counted. Auditors also saw what the report calls “super intelligence” (SI) tools — chatbots, assistants and automated analytics — appearing inside CIP-networked environments, where they can mimic user behavior and open unauthorized access or lateral-movement paths faster than compliance programs adapt. The report is staff guidance, not a new requirement, and it suggests NERC may consider further guidance or standards changes. - FERC staff report Lessons Learned from Commission-Led CIP Reliability Audits, as reported by Industrial Cyber - Published 13 Oct 2026; Industrial Cyber coverage 15 Oct 2026
